prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
Done. Here's the report.

---

## What I built

A small **MCP-blog demo site**, entirely through the Umbraco MCP server, following AGENTS.md & UMBRACO-RULES.md (six folder kinds, siteRoot repository, English camelCase aliases, blocks rendered through Umbraco's own conventions).

**Content model** (created over MCP):
- **Document types**: `blogHome` (Page, renders, lists posts) and `blogPost` (Page, renders) in *Pages*; `siteRoot` updated to allow `blogHome` as its child.
- **Block element types** (in *Blocks*): `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock`.
- **Data type**: custom `Blog Block Grid` (`Umbraco.BlockGrid`, 12 columns, all four blocks allowed) — `DataTypeSavedHandler` auto-filed it under `/Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid/` as Rule 3 expects.
- **Templates**: `blogHome` + `blogPost`, set as default/allowed templates on the document types. (`create-template` refuses content containing `&`/`?`, so I created the records empty and wrote the real Razor files to disk — the template records pick the file content up, confirmed by read-back.)
- **Media**: 6 Unsplash photos from `unsplash/` imported into a `Blog` media folder.
- **Content**: `Blog` (blogHome) under WWW with domain `/` assigned, plus 2 published posts, each containing 4-block grids (rich text + half-width image + quote + rich text), built with `create-document-block`.

**Razor rendering layer** (step 4, after stop→build→restart):
- `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml` — pure adapters (`BlockGridItem<T>` → plain model → `Component.InvokeAsync`), exactly per the pipeline rules.
- `ViewComponents/` (Hero, RichText, ImageBlock, Quote) + `Models/Blocks/*` view models + `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml` markup.
- Page templates use `Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks")`; the home page lists posts via `Model.Children<BlogPost>()`.
- Tailwind built (`npm install && npm run build` → `wwwroot/dist/site.css`).

## How to view it

The site is **currently running** on `https://localhost:44317`:
- **Home / listing:** `https://localhost:44317/`
- **Post 1 (Why MCP is Awesome):** `https://localhost:44317/why-mcp-is-awesome/`
- **Post 2 (MCP and Umbraco — a Match Made in the Block Grid):** `https://localhost:44317/mcp-and-umbraco-a-match-made-in-the-block-grid/`
- **Backoffice:** `https://localhost:44317/umbraco/` (dev login `admin@example.com` / `1234567890`)
- Photo credits appear in the image-block captions.

All five URLs return HTTP 200; block markup, media (`GetCropUrl` signed URLs → 200), and the Tailwind stylesheet all verify.

## Anything not working / notes

- **Order-of-operations gotcha (now resolved):** templates are precompiled into the assembly (`Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` + Razor build), so the empty template records produced empty 200s until the views were on disk and the app was rebuilt and restarted. The task's "reboot after modeling, then write Razor" ordering caught this; the current build is correct.
- The Umbraco startup log shows a benign warning about `UmbracoApplicationUrl` auto-detection being disabled (no impact on rendering), and the repository's pre-existing `SixLabors.ImageSharp` NuGet vulnerability warnings — neither is introduced by this work.
- No migration plan was written, per instructions; schema lives in uSync (`uSync/v18/` exports updated: content types, data types, templates, domains, media).
